newsitem.title: USA: Toys R Us posts strong Q2 amid higher sales.
newsitem.headline: Toys R Us posts strong Q2 amid higher sales.

text.p: Toys R Us Inc on Monday attributed its strong second quarter results to higher sales of video games and action figures, and lower interest expense.
The company earned $36.7 million, or $0.13 a share, in the quarter ended August 2, easily beating Wall Street's projections.
A May 22 First Call consensus estimate of 22 analysts had put the company's earnings at $0.11 a share.
Quarterly sales increased 15 percent to $1.99 billion from $1.74 billion in 1996, while U.S. same-store sales rose four percent for the quarter and six percent in the first half.

"These sales gains are attributable to the continued strength of the video game business as well as strong sales of action figures, plush and outdoor playsets. In addition, the virtual pet craze spurred by Tamagotchi has further increased customer traffic in our stores," the company said.

The company said its Kids R Us division posted higher comparable sales for the quarter, but its Babies R Us same-store sales decreased. It added stores in Canada and the United Kingdom posted double-digit same-store sales growth for the quarter and the first half.
Toys R Us said lower interest expense due to improved cash flow and expense control also contributed to its second-quarter earnings.
The company's stock closed at 33 Friday.
